title: 10 Kg Fat Kam Hua... Woh Gaya Kahan?
title_options: 10 Kg Fat Kam Hua... Woh Gaya Kahan?
Jab Aap Weight Kam Karte Ho, Fat Jaata Kahan Hai?
Weight Loss Ka Chhupa Sach: Fat Saans Se Nikalta Hai
summary: This video explains, using the 2014 BMJ study by Ruben Meerman and Andrew Brown, that when a person loses 10 kg of fat, about 8.4 kg physically leaves the body as exhaled carbon dioxide and 1.6 kg becomes water excreted through urine, sweat and breath. It walks through the law of conservation of mass, the biological journey of fat from fat cells to mitochondria to the lungs, and the real stoichiometric numbers behind it, correcting the common myth that fat simply converts into energy or heat.

facts.fact: BMJ published Ruben Meerman and Andrew Brown's paper 'When somebody loses weight, where does the fat go?' in its Christmas issue on 16 December 2014.
Most doctors, dietitians and personal trainers surveyed wrongly believed fat converts into energy or heat, which violates the law of conservation of mass.
Complete oxidation of 10 kg of human fat requires 29 kg of inhaled oxygen and produces 28 kg of carbon dioxide and 11 kg of water.
When 10 kg of fat is lost, 8.4 kg (84%) leaves the body as exhaled carbon dioxide and 1.6 kg (16%) becomes water.
The lungs are the primary excretory organ for weight loss; the water formed is excreted via urine, faeces, sweat, breath and tears.
An average triglyceride (body fat) molecule has the chemical formula C55H104O6, first described by Hirsch and colleagues in 1960.
At rest, a 70 kg person exhales about 200 ml of CO2 in 12 breaths per minute, each breath releasing 33 mg of CO2 containing 8.9 mg of carbon.
Over 24 hours of sleep, rest and light activity, an average person loses about 203 grams of carbon from the body.
Replacing one hour of rest with one hour of moderate exercise like jogging increases metabolic rate sevenfold, removing an extra 40 g of carbon and raising the daily total by about 20% to 240 g.
Standing up and getting dressed more than doubles resting metabolic rate; going for a walk roughly triples it.
Metabolising 100 grams of fat consumes 290 grams of oxygen and produces 280 grams of carbon dioxide plus 110 grams of water.
The law of conservation of mass states mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; it was conclusively demonstrated by French chemist Antoine Lavoisier around 1789.
facts.source: Nature Scitable, 2014; Wikipedia, Conservation of Mass

facts.fact: Carbon exhaled after fat loss comes from food made by plants within months or years, not from fossil fuels, so it does not add to climate change the way burning fossil carbon does.
Triglycerides (stored fat) are broken down by the enzyme lipase in a process called lipolysis into one glycerol molecule and three fatty acid molecules.

youtube.title: 10 Kg Fat Kam Hua Toh Woh Gaya Kahan? Science Ka Jawab
youtube.description:
Jab hum weight loss karte hain, toh asli sawaal yeh hai ki woh 'lost' mass jaata kahan hai. Is video mein hum 2014 ke BMJ study (Ruben Meerman aur Andrew Brown, University of New South Wales) ke real numbers ke saath samjhate hain ki 10 kg fat lose karne par 8.4 kg carbon dioxide ban kar lungs se exhale hota hai, aur 1.6 kg paani ban kar urine, sweat aur breath se nikalta hai. Hum law of conservation of mass se shuru karte hain, fat cell se lekar mitochondria tak ka 3D body journey dikhate hain, aur asli calculation step by step samjhate hain.
